target.title: Roll Claude reset date forward across the year boundary
target.body:
ClaudeStatusProbe.parseResetDate handles its two date+time branches ("MMM d, h:mma" and hour-only variants) by returning the parsed date as-is. Those formats carry no year token, so DateFormatter.defaultDate = now fills in the current year. When the reset month/day is earlier in the calendar than now - e.g. a "Jan 2" reset string read on Dec 31 - the result lands roughly a year in the past instead of a few hours in the future.

A past resetsAt is not harmless: UsageFormatter.resetCountdownDescription clamps timeIntervalSince(now) with max(0, ...) so the countdown shows "now"/"0h", and widget "is this window active" checks (resetsAt.map { $0 > now }) treat the window as already expired. The menu bar/widget then show the quota as reset hours before it actually is.

The two time-only branches directly below already roll forward (by a day), and the sibling CodexStatusProbe.parseResetDate already guards this exact case with bumpYearIfNeeded. This applies the same guard to Claude's date+time branches for consistency.

Testing: added a regression test that crosses the year boundary (now = Dec 31, reset text = "Resets Jan 2, 3:00am (UTC)"). It fails on the old code (parses to Jan 2 of the current year, ~a year in the past) and passes after the fix (Jan 2 next year, in the future). All existing Claude reset-parsing tests still pass.
